title: Z-variable commutes with dualization
statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $p$ be a deterministic disjointness protocol on inputs of length $n$, and let $\omega$ be a sample from the hard distribution. Forming the $Z$-variable — the packaged record consisting of the transcript of $p$ on the input generated by $\omega$, together with the special coordinate, Alice's bits strictly before it, and Bob's bits strictly after it — commutes with dualization: the $Z$-variable of the dual protocol evaluated at the dualized sample coincides with the dualization of the $Z$-variable of $p$ at $\omega$. That is,
\[
Z\bigl(p^\ast,\ \omega^\ast\bigr) \;=\; \bigl(Z(p,\omega)\bigr)^\ast,
\]
where $p^\ast$ is the protocol obtained by interchanging Alice and Bob and reversing both coordinate sets, $\omega^\ast$ is the sample obtained by swapping Alice's and Bob's bits and reversing the coordinate order, and $(\,\cdot\,)^\ast$ on $Z$-values is the corresponding recoding.
hypotheses_covered: p is a disjointness protocol of length n
replaced: The $Z$ variable for the dual protocol and hard sample is the recoded original $Z$.
